messages.subject: outliers
parts:
Hi group,

you are so helpful :)

what is the best way to remove outliers from a time series?

I was looking for something like this (moving average), but it didnt do much to my data
https://anomaly.io/moving-median-robust-anomaly/

2 questions: 

1. how do you loop over 7 files of csv? in each file there are time readings of 4 sensors. (attached one of them)

2. suggestions on the best way to remove the outliers. I have 15 min reading of a sensor. the readings fail sometimes. and I want to remove the failures. some of the sensors its more than half of the readings. 


thank you for all the help,

enjoy your weekend :)

messages.author: 5f533b50135a7f86
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: outliers
parts:
Hi Hanna, 

1. Assuming you want your loop to load the files and combine them into one big dataframe, try something like
files = list.files(data_dir)
files_with_path = str_c(data_dir, files)
dataf = map_dfr(files_with_path, read_csv, .id = ’sourcefile’)

This uses tidyverse packages.  map_dfr is a version of map (so takes the elements in the first argument and applies the function in the second argument) that combines the results into a single dataframe.  The .id argument adds a column corresponding to the item’s name in the list.  

2. First, I’m assuming you have good reasons for thinking these are sensor failures and should be trimmed.  (You probably do, I just wouldn’t be a good DSI postdoc if I didn’t do some finger wagging about trimming data.)  

Second, could you say more about how you want to identify the outliers?  Just a few approaches that come to mind:  
 - based on threshold values (larger than x is an outlier)
- more than x standard deviations from the mean value
- change in value or total variation over x seconds is greater than y
- before the first x seconds

Some of these will work fairly differently from others in R.  

Cheers, 
Dan

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: outliers
parts:
the sensors measure daily water content, and have an oscillating (so it can't be only grater than). when the sensor working correct the values somewhere around -10 to -30.  any jump of more than 10 units is a failure. 
also, sometimes there is more than 50 wrong readings. (if the sensor wasn't serviced on time). can the code take last good readings for the moving average? or how it deals with a lot of NA's?
In matlab I would say somthing like this: the current cell shouldnt be greater or lower than the average of the x number of the cells before it, times 10 percent . if does replace with NA (or the average of these x cells) how would you translate into R?

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: outliers
parts: Just have time for a quick suggestion:  Using functions like summarize(), create a new dataframe of moving averages (time t gets the average of itself + (x-1) proceeding observations).  Add a lag, so time t gets the average of x proceeding observations.  Join this to your observation dataframe, so the observation at time t and be compared to the average of x proceeding observations.
